body: Proprietary agent personas, role contracts, and system instructions constitute core enterprise IP. Shipping them as raw markdown or JSON on customer filesystems (on-prem/OEM) exposes Product Forge's competitive reasoning logic to reverse engineering and direct extraction. This item establishes the asset compiler and runtime decryptor to keep prompt IP secure.
_note: Full authoring of context, epic, and ACs

brief.why: Raw plaintext prompt files and markdown instructions on distributed customer filesystems create critical reverse engineering and IP theft vulnerability.
brief.problem: Agent system instructions, system prompts, and tool calling definitions are currently stored as plaintext or markdown files, creating high vulnerability to reverse-engineering, prompt extraction, and IP theft in on-prem and edge distributions.
brief.what_adds: Prompt and Persona Asset Compiler providing offline tokenization, bytecode encryption with AES-256-GCM, and transparent runtime decrypt-on-invocation in native Go.
brief.who_feels: Enterprise customers, on-prem deployment operators, platform security officers, and Product Forge commercial maintainers

label: PF Backlog 685
risks: Key management complexity in air-gapped sovereign environments mitigated via licensing key derivation.
title: Prompt and Persona Asset Compiler: secure compilation and runtime encryption for proprietary agent instructions

review.reasons: Senior Enterprise Architect Review: Aligned with ADR-0001, BI-PF-0387, and BI-PF-0388 single-source compiled delivery baseline. Sensitive prompt encryption and runtime decryption logic lands in native Go (go/promptcompiler) to prevent IP leakage; build tooling resides in scripts/dev/prompt_compiler.py adhering to config/language-rule.json. Approved for implementation under EPIC A (BI-PF-0390).

impact_review.recommendation: Implement core AES-256-GCM cipher and runtime decryption in Go (go/promptcompiler/); build-time CLI in scripts/dev/prompt_compiler.py.

impact_review.claim: API CHECK: packaging and offline asset compilation capability
impact_review.recommendation: Offline build-time compiler CLI and native Go runtime library; no unauthenticated HTTP API route required.

impact_review.claim: AC-1: AES-256-GCM authenticated cipher with runtime key derivation
impact_review.recommendation: Implement tokenization and AES-256-GCM authenticated cipher with HKDF key derivation.

impact_review.claim: AC-2: Shipped customer packages contain zero readable system prompt files
impact_review.recommendation: Enforce packaging scanner that fails closed if raw .md prompt files are detected in distribution payloads.

impact_review.claim: AC-3: In-memory runtime transparent decryption with zero disk leakage
impact_review.recommendation: Load encrypted asset bundles directly into memory and verify zero scratch file disk writes.

assumptions: Standard AES-256-GCM with 96-bit random nonce and 128-bit authentication tag is the enterprise standard for prompt asset protection.
The runtime decryption key is derived from the platform instance entitlement key / environment master key (via HKDF-SHA256).
Decrypted prompt text is loaded directly into the execution context in memory; no temporary decrypted files are ever written to disk.
Shipped commercial distributions (enterprise, on-prem, oem, saas) must fail-closed if raw prompt markdown files exist in the distribution payload.
divergences: None: Extends canonical A3/A5 packaging pipeline and implements runtime decryption in native Go without creating duplicate engines.
existing_path: Prompt & persona definitions: config/persona.json:1, config/agent-hierarchy.json:1, templates/prompts/
Shipped language rule: config/language-rule.json:4-8 (shipped_roots: core/, api/, adapters/)
prior_decisions: ADR-0001 / BI-PF-0388: Shipped editions use compiled artifacts; never raw .py; one source, many editions.
BI-PF-0387: Single-source delivery baseline; new shipped/sensitive logic lands in native Go (go/ directory).
BI-PF-0398: A3 compiled packaging pipeline + NO-RAW-.py release gate (enforces zero raw code leakage).
BI-PF-0399: A5 Runtime Dependency Compiler (composes EAP + profiles + OS/arch into runtime composition).

summary: Build an asset compilation and encryption pipeline that compiles agent prompts and persona templates into Go binary assets via embed.FS or encrypted asset packages with runtime license-key-derived decryption.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/agent_capabilities.py, core/agent_card_loader.py, core/agent_hierarchy.py, core/agent_ledger.py

approach: Implement compile_prompts() pipeline that packages prompt markdown files into encrypted .bin bundles and catalogs them in EAP manifest.
rollback: Disable prompt compilation in packaging flags to fall back to standard asset packaging.

decisions.note: Senior Enterprise Architect approval: Prompt and Persona Asset Compiler approved for implementation. Native Go AES-256-GCM encryption with HKDF key derivation, build-time packaging compiler, and zero raw markdown prompt leakage in commercial packages.

objective: Build a secure prompt compiler and runtime packaging layer that compiles proprietary agent instructions into encrypted asset bundles in EAP distributions.

applicability.reason: Specification for prompt tokenization, encryption format, and packaging
Offline build-time compilation CLI and internal in-memory Go library without public HTTP routes
Encrypted binary asset bundle (.pfa) binary schema and header layout
PF_PROMPT_KEY and PF_PROMPT_BUNDLE configuration environment contract
Sub-10ms bundle decryption latency and zero scratch disk write enforcement
Reverse engineering protection and authenticated cipher tamper rejection
Build-time packaging feature; no legacy database table backfill required
Disable prompt compilation flag in packaging pipeline to revert cleanly
Structured JSON logging with compilation duration, asset counts, and SHA-256 digests
Backend packaging and compiler tooling with no end-user web UI elements
Operates on internal prompt assets and developer definitions; no customer PII
Staged implementation: Go cipher package -> build-time compiler CLI -> packaging leakage scanner -> e2e tests
Automated pytest and Go test suite validating encryption, decryption, and leakage absence

api_impact.reason: Offline build-time packaging CLI and Go in-memory runtime library; zero unauthenticated HTTP attack surface.

requirements: Prompt asset compiler tokenizes and encrypts persona definitions using AES-256-GCM authenticated cipher with runtime key derivation.
Shipped customer packages contain zero readable system prompt files or plaintext markdown instructions in distributions.
Runtime agent adapter transparently decrypts and loads compiled prompt bundles in memory with zero plaintext disk leakage.
invariants: Decrypted plaintext prompts exist only in volatile heap memory; never written to filesystem.
Tampered ciphertext bundles fail closed immediately upon authentication tag check.
Key derivation incorporates salt and domain separation context (HKDF-SHA256).

contracts.api: Offline CLI and Go library; no external HTTP routes exposed.
contracts.db: No relational database dependencies required for asset compilation.
contracts.files: Compiles raw markdown prompts into encrypted .pfa binary bundle with magic bytes PFA1.
contracts.config: PF_PROMPT_KEY (minimum 32 bytes) and PF_PROMPT_BUNDLE file location path.

failure_matrix.recovery: re-encrypt bundle with matching master key

failure_matrix.condition: plaintext prompt detected in commercial distribution
failure_matrix.behavior: packaging gate fails closed and halts release build
failure_matrix.recovery: exclude raw prompt markdown from distribution payload

design_pack.security: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with 96-bit random nonce and 128-bit authentication tag; zero disk leakage.
design_pack.observability: Structured logs recording bundle compilation time, input count, payload size, and bundle SHA-256 digest.
design_pack.performance: Sub-10ms bundle decryption latency for complete 50-persona catalog.
design_pack.rollout: Stage 1: Go cipher package. Stage 2: Build CLI compiler. Stage 3: Packaging integration and verification tests.
design_pack.rollback: Disable prompt compilation flag in packaging pipeline to revert to raw asset packaging.
decisions: Standard AES-256-GCM with HKDF key derivation selected for tamper-evident encryption.
Single compiled binary bundle format (.pfa) with magic header PFA1.
guardrails: Fail closed on authentication tag mismatch.
Fail closed on any raw prompt file detected in commercial packaging output.
learnings: Storing prompts as raw markdown files on client disks poses high IP theft risk.

implementation_controls.control: AES-256-GCM authenticated cipher encryption of prompt assets
Fail-closed release gate verifying absence of raw prompt files
Runtime in-memory transparent decryption with zero disk leakage
Compilation telemetry and SHA-256 provenance tracking
Commercial distribution isolation ensuring zero plaintext prompt leaks

requirements.title: Prompt asset compiler tokenizes and encrypts persona definitions using AES-256-GCM authenticated cipher
preconditions: Proprietary agent prompt files and master key present
requirements.trigger: Execution of prompt compiler CLI or packaging pipeline step
inputs: Directory of prompt files, persona definitions, master key string
outputs: Encrypted binary asset bundle with header, nonce, auth tag, and payload
requirements.idempotency: Deterministic ciphertext generation with reproducible HKDF info
edge_cases: Corrupted header or altered auth tag aborts decryption fail-closed
acceptance: Given a directory of agent prompt definitions, When the prompt compiler executes, Then persona definitions are compiled into an encrypted asset bundle using AES-256-GCM.

requirements.title: Shipped customer packages contain zero readable system prompt files or plaintext markdown instructions
requirements.trigger: Package verification gate execution prior to release artifact sealing
outputs: Verification pass report or leakage failure list
data_rules: Zero unencrypted .md prompt files or plaintext persona JSON in commercial outputs
edge_cases: Nested subdirectories or zip archives inspected recursively
acceptance: Given a compiled commercial distribution package, When the packaging leakage scanner runs, Then zero plaintext system prompt files or readable instructions are found.

requirements.title: Runtime agent adapter transparently decrypts and loads compiled prompt bundles in memory with zero disk leakage
preconditions: Encrypted bundle file and valid runtime entitlement key present
requirements.trigger: Agent runtime initialization requesting persona or instruction text
inputs: Encrypted bundle stream or file path, runtime key
outputs: In-memory agent persona instructions and prompt dictionary
requirements.idempotency: Decryption is stateless and can be invoked repeatedly
data_rules: Decrypted prompt memory retained only in heap; zero disk scratch writes
edge_cases: Tampered ciphertext raises authenticated cipher error immediately
acceptance: Given an encrypted prompt bundle, When agent runtime loads persona instructions, Then decrypted text is loaded directly in memory without writing temporary files to disk.

operation_matrix.expected: Encrypted bundle generated with SHA-256 digest

config_contract.name: PF_PROMPT_BUNDLE
config_contract.valid_values: valid file path ending in .pfa or .bin
